report.clinical_summary: The patient has been managing HIV for several years, currently on Triumeq (started 3 years ago). They're experiencing more intense fatigue and headaches over the past few months, which is affecting their ability to keep up with daily tasks and work. They've been non-adherent (missing doses, taking drug holidays) due to medication side effects (headaches, nausea). They still believe the medication helps suppress the virus but feel it's 'not doing enough' and are considering switching medications. They view HIV as a lifelong condition but have learned to manage it. They have mixed feelings about medications in general, concerned about long-term effects, and sometimes wonder if doctors prescribe too readily.

evidence.quote: It's been a struggle to just keep up with everyday things. I'm having trouble keeping my usual schedule and getting as much done at work as I used to. I feel like everything is piling up
